title: Deploy Spotlight weeklet checkpad + release notes (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact week-long runbook ("weeklet") for the Deploy Spotlight release window. Intended for small-surface launches where we gradually ramp an opt-in cohort, validate latency/cost regressions, and exercise model-routing fallbacks. Not a canonical mega-launch playbook — focused on fast iteration, tight telemetry, and clear ownership.

Status notes:
- Draft: core checklist assembled, waiting on SRE shift staffing confirmation and final canary traffic target numbers.
- TODO: confirm dedicated capacity thresholds with infra (ticket JIRA-RELEASE-3421).

High level rollout goals:
- Ramp to 10% of production traffic over 72 hours, gated on: error rate (<0.5%), 95th latency within +20% of baseline, token cost delta < 8%.
- Validate KV-cache effectiveness and residual cold-starts with sampled traces.
- Test auto-fallback to quantized model variant if GPU pool saturates.

Preflight (72–24h) checklist (owner tags in parentheses):
- Verify smoke images and docker tags match release branch (Marcus).
- Confirm canary routing policy set in traffic-router and documented in Confluence (Priya).
- Autoscaling policy review: min/max instances and burst settings (SRE lead).
- Alerting sanity: ensure burn-rate + latency SLO alerts are enabled and thresholded for this release (Diego).
- Security quick-check: ensure key rotation not scheduled during window; audit log sampling enabled (Security).
- Canary dataset: prepare 3 prompts (latency-sensitive / hallucination-sensitive / throughput burner) and pin IDs for quality checks (ML QA).
- Communication: announce watch window in #deploys, set calendar invites for 24/72h checkpoints (Avery).

Launch day hour-by-hour (abridged) — day 0 (owner in parens):
- H-30: final quick status: infra green, repo green, release notes posted to Confluence (Avery).
- H0: shift flip - canary starts at 0.5% traffic routed to model vX (SRE + FE).
- H0+30m: smoke tests (end-to-end): top-of-stack call, KV cache hit rate, and streaming path validation (QA).
- H1: telemetry snapshot: token cost, per-request latency distribution, 5xx counts, model quality quickcheck (telemetry lead).
- H4: decision checkpoint 1: move to 2% if no gating trips (Release Engineer).
- H24: decision checkpoint 2: move to 5% contingent on quality signals and cost (Release Engineer + PM).
- H48: decision checkpoint 3: move to 10% OR rollback to last-stable if any gating condition fails.

Gating conditions (explicit):
- Stability: rolling 15m error rate >0.5% triggers immediate pause and audit.
- Latency: 95th percentile exceeds baseline by >20% for two consecutive 30m windows -> pause.
- Cost: token cost per 1k tokens increases >8% sustained over 1h -> hold and investigate.
- Quality: model hallucination rate on the pinned prompt set increases by >5 percentage points -> hold and run regression evaluation.

Rollback plan (fast path):
- If immediate rollback required, flip traffic-router to last-stable model alias (0-5m flip).
- Execute hotpatch to config store to remove canary entries and re-route any lingering sessions (Release Engineer).
- Notify #oncall, customer-success, and product about rollback rationale and affected cohorts.
- Post-rollback postmortem template: timeline, trigger, root-cause hypothesis, mitigation steps.

Telemetry & sampling strategy:
- High-volume metrics (latency, errors, cpu/gpu utilization) at 30s resolution.
- Request-level traces sampled 1% overall, but 100% for the pinned prompt set and any requests hitting fallback path.
- KV-cache instrumentation: log hit/miss and serialized size per request for 100% of canary traffic.
- Cost sampling: attribute tokens to route/model and compute 1h rolling cost delta.
- Quality sampling: store outputs for the three pinned prompts, annotate with manual QA labels.

Operational quick reference (cheatpad):
- Rollforward command: opsctl route set --alias model-x --percent 2 --cohort canary (ops/ghe).
- Kill problematic nodes: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets (SRE).
- Snapshot logs: make sure to create timeboxed log-extract in GCS with tag "deploy-spotlight-<date>" before any global changes.

Staffing & rotations (weeklet):
- Coverage model: primary + backup on-call for SRE, Release Engineer, Telemetry, ML QA. 
- Nights: single SRE + release engineer on pager for reduced traffic windows.
- 24h checkpoints require both Release Engineer and Telemetry lead to be available for decision.

Release notes (draft) — public-facing summary:
Title: "Spotlight release: Model vX (staged rollout)"
Summary: "We are deploying Model vX to a small cohort to validate latency, cost and output fidelity under production traffic patterns. This rollout will be gradual and monitored; the experience for most users will be unchanged while we complete the validation window."
What’s new: "- Backend: updated KV cache eviction and more aggressive prefix coalescing. - Model: vX uses updated attention kernels and a quantization-friendly weight layout for throughput gains."
Known limitations: "- Edge cases exist for very long context sequences (>32k) where cold-start latency may be higher. - Some internal metrics may undercount initial KV cache effectiveness until warmup completes."
Rollout plan summary: "Incremental ramp to 10% over 72 hours with explicit gating on error-rate, latency, and cost. We will automatically rollback if thresholds are exceeded."
How to contact us: "#deploys Slack for internal; support@redwood-inference.com for customer-facing issues (include time and request id)."

Post-release (24–72h) workstream items:
- Telemetry deep-dive: examine 95/99p latencies by region and model shard.
- Cost spike forensic: correlate token composition, temperature, and batch sizes at time of spikes.
- Quality regression harness: run full eval suite on a larger prompt corpus (ML).
- Follow-up tickets: list observed anomalies, owner, priority, target date.

Notes to self / loose thoughts: 
- Consider adding an automated canary quality checklist that runs evals every 4 hours and posts a tiny dashboard snapshot in the #deploys thread.
- Might be useful to pin a canary-only debug endpoint that returns KV cache miss context for quick triage.
- If we repeatedly flip routes for transient GPU OOMs, we need a preemptive throttle at the scheduler level to avoid oscillation.

Attachments & references:
- Confluence page: CONFLUENCE-RT/Spotlight-Launch-Plan (linked above)
- Canary PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/199 — contains config changes and autoscaler hints.
- Post-deploy retro template: CONFLUENCE-RT/Deploy-Retrospective-Template

Open action items (owners):
- Marcus: confirm docker tag immutability and push timeline.
- Priya: finalize routing policy and add explicit fallback testcases.
- Diego: create alert runbook snippet for new latency alert variant.
- Avery: publish draft release notes to shared drive and ping stakeholder reviewers.

End of weeklet draft. Keep this as the single source-of-truth for the week-of-watch. Update in-place as decisions are made — prefer small, timestamped edits rather than new docs to preserve the watch timeline.

Quick changelog: 2026-09-15 created initial skeleton (Avery). 2026-09-17 added gating thresholds and telemetry sampling (Diego). 2026-09-21 updated staffing roster and release note wording (Marcus/Priya).
